title: Gentle Blinking
description: A simple exercise to restore healthy blink patterns during screen use.
purpose: Prolonged screen focus often reduces blink rate. This exercise helps you practice full, deliberate blinks to keep your eyes comfortable.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.instruction: Sit comfortably and look straight ahead. Relax your shoulders and unclench your jaw.

steps.title: Full blink
steps.instruction: Close your eyes gently but completely. Hold for 1 second. Open slowly.

steps.title: Repeat
steps.instruction: Blink gently 10 more times at a natural pace. Focus on fully closing your eyelids each time.

steps.title: Rest
steps.instruction: Close your eyes and relax for a few seconds. Notice how your eyes feel.

safety_note: If you feel any discomfort, stop and blink naturally. This exercise should feel comfortable.
completion_message: Well done. Your eyes should feel more comfortable.

title: Relaxed Blink Routine
description: A gentle blink exercise combined with relaxation to reduce eye tension.
purpose: Combines deliberate blinking with brief relaxation to help reset your blink pattern and reduce accumulated tension.
recommended_frequency: Once per hour during extended screen use

steps.title: Settle in
steps.instruction: Close your eyes and take two slow, deep breaths.

steps.title: Gentle blinks
steps.instruction: Open your eyes and blink softly 15 times. Do not squeeze — just let your eyelids meet gently.

steps.title: Hold and rest
steps.instruction: Close your eyes again. Hold them closed gently for 5 seconds, then relax completely for 10 seconds.

steps.title: Repeat cycle
steps.instruction: Open your eyes and blink softly 10 more times at a comfortable pace.

steps.title: Final rest
steps.instruction: Close your eyes for a final moment and notice the difference in comfort.

safety_note: Keep the blinks gentle. If your eyes feel strained, shorten the exercise.
completion_message: Routine complete. Your blink pattern should feel more natural now.

title: Look Into the Distance
description: Shift your focus to a distant object to relax your eye muscles.
purpose: Your ciliary muscles stay contracted during near-focus work. Looking at distant objects allows these muscles to relax, which can reduce eye fatigue.

steps.title: Find a target
steps.instruction: Look up from your screen and find an object at least 20 feet (6 meters) away — a window, a wall decoration, or anything across the room.

steps.title: Focus softly
steps.instruction: Gaze at the distant object without straining. Let your eyes relax into the focus. Blink naturally.

steps.title: Scan gently
steps.instruction: Slowly shift your gaze between two distant points. Move your eyes, not your head.

steps.title: Return
steps.instruction: Look back at your screen. Notice how your eyes feel after the break.

safety_note: Do not force your focus. The distant view should feel easy and comfortable.
completion_message: Distance viewing complete. Your eye muscles have had a chance to relax.

title: Short Visual Rest
description: A brief eyes-closed rest to reduce accumulated visual fatigue.
purpose: Closing your eyes gives them a complete rest from light and focus effort. Even a short rest can help reduce feelings of visual fatigue.
recommended_frequency: Every hour or when eyes feel tired

steps.title: Pause
steps.instruction: Stop what you are doing and set aside your screen.

steps.title: Close your eyes
steps.instruction: Close your eyes gently. Do not press on your eyelids.

steps.title: Breathe and rest
steps.instruction: Take slow, deep breaths. Let your eyes rest in complete darkness for about 40 seconds.

steps.title: Open gradually
steps.instruction: Open your eyes slowly. Blink a few times before returning to your screen.

safety_note: If you feel uncomfortable with your eyes closed for extended periods, shorten the rest.
completion_message: Rest complete. Your eyes should feel refreshed.

title: Near-to-Far Focus
description: Alternate focusing between near and far objects to exercise your accommodation.
purpose: Your eyes continuously adjust focus between near and far objects. This exercise practices that transition, which can help reduce focus-related fatigue.
recommended_frequency: Once per hour during focused work

steps.title: Hold your thumb out
steps.instruction: Extend your arm and hold your thumb about 10 inches (25 cm) from your face.

steps.title: Focus near
steps.instruction: Focus on your thumbnail for 5 seconds. Notice the details on your thumb.

steps.title: Focus far
steps.instruction: Shift your gaze to an object at least 20 feet away. Focus on it for 5 seconds.

steps.title: Repeat cycle
steps.instruction: Alternate between your thumb and the distant object 8 more times. Move your eyes smoothly, without jerking.

steps.title: Rest
steps.instruction: Lower your hand and blink gently a few times.

safety_note: Move your focus smoothly between near and far. If you feel any eye strain, stop and rest.
completion_message: Focus shifting complete. Your accommodation muscles have been gently exercised.

title: Guided Visual Break
description: A complete guided break combining distance viewing, blinking, and rest.
purpose: This exercise combines several techniques into one short session, giving your eyes a comprehensive break from screen focus.

steps.title: Step away
steps.instruction: Push back from your desk. Roll your shoulders back once.

steps.title: Distance viewing
steps.instruction: Look at something across the room. Hold your gaze there and blink naturally for 20 seconds.

steps.title: Gentle blinks
steps.instruction: Close your eyes and blink softly 10 times. Keep your face relaxed.

steps.title: Eye movement
steps.instruction: Open your eyes and slowly look up, then down, then left, then right. Move gently without straining.

steps.title: Final rest
steps.instruction: Close your eyes for 15 seconds. Breathe naturally.

steps.title: Return
steps.instruction: Open your eyes. You are ready to continue.

safety_note: Move your eyes gently throughout. Never force a stretch or push through discomfort.
completion_message: Break complete. Your eyes have rested and reset.
